response: About two months ago I was visiting Las Vegas to see my mother. She had suffered a stroke the previous month, and I needed to be there for her. When I arrived at her house on a Tuesday evening, I embraced her tightly in the living room. During my week-long stay, we spent considerable time together at her apartment and at the rehabilitation center. The neurologist confirmed her recovery was progressing well, though she would need to follow a strict Mediterranean diet and complete physical therapy three times weekly. I felt both relieved and emotional seeing her determination. We watched movies together, took short walks around the neighborhood, and discussed my relocation plans. I've already started looking at apartments in the Henderson area, about fifteen minutes from her place. This visit reinforced how important it is to maintain close family bonds. I'm grateful for the support system in place and look forward to being nearby to help with her continued recovery.

She had experienced occasional shortness of breath while climbing stairs, which she'd attributed to age. Dr. Patterson, whom she'd seen for eight years, explained the blockages required intervention. Buddy had been my constant companion for eleven years. Losing him shattered me completely.

I had also arranged for the girl he liked to be watching, which made him even angrier when he lost. He reacted as though the result were a personal humiliation, stopping just short of throwing himself onto the floor in frustration. I honestly wondered whether he had been deliberately playing below his usual level, because the match felt strangely one-sided. Still, he had expected to win, and his embarrassment turned into a dramatic tantrum when I beat him in front of her.

response: In June, I attended a family reunion held at the New Jersey home of my cousin’s former husband. At the previous year’s gathering, he had driven to our home in New York, picked up my partner and me, and taken us to the reunion. This year, one of the cousins helping organize the event said she would try to find transportation for us, but she could not arrange it. Consequently, we traveled by public transport: first taking the subway to Manhattan’s Port Authority, then a bus into New Jersey, and finally calling my cousin after we arrived so that someone could collect us. The journey was expected to take roughly two hours, and I checked Google Maps beforehand to plan the route.

response: Last July, my husband and I traveled to Arizona to visit his parents, something we had wanted to do for a long time. His mother had struggled with memory loss for several years and had only recently moved from her home into assisted living. During the preceding year, her memory had deteriorated so much that she could no longer manage a telephone conversation or remember to speak into the receiver. response: Five months ago, I received a kidney transplant, and I remain deeply grateful for it. Before the transplant, dialysis made daily life extremely difficult. I could not work full-time, depended on state health benefits, and spent hours each day connected to a machine. The situation was exhausting and discouraging, and at my lowest point I seriously considered ending my life. Since receiving the kidney, I have regained control of my routine and can work full-time again. I have more time and energy for friends and family, and I am enjoying my hobbies in ways I could not before. Instead of arranging my days around dialysis, I can go hiking, take vacations, and participate in ordinary activities. The transplant has allowed me to feel engaged with life again.

response: Dear Diary, Eight weeks have passed since my husband and I visited Niagara Falls, and I am finally ready to write about the frightening part of that trip. I have already described the enjoyable moments, the shopping, and how impressive the Falls looked, but I left out what happened during dinner on our first evening. Something occurred there that resulted in me worrying about the law and looking over my shoulder, afraid that the authorities might reconsider the situation and arrest me. I am not someone who normally gets into trouble, which made the experience especially upsetting. Perhaps the noise and force of the rushing water had left me overstimulated: I could still feel the spray against my arms and the sensation made my hair stand up. The trip was memorable for both its beauty and that unsettling personal fall.

response: Several months ago, a group of friends and I went kayaking on the Yadkin River, something we do fairly regularly. This outing, however, became much more challenging than normal. My brother’s girlfriend had consumed too much alcohol. Close to the end of the trip, she jumped out of her kayak to cool down in the water, but the shock of the cold water seemed to intensify her intoxication. From then on, the trip turned chaotic. She repeatedly tipped or swamped her kayak, perhaps thirty times, and I became completely worn out helping her. Finishing the last quarter mile took more than an hour. When we finally reached the takeout point, I felt almost entirely unable to do anything else.

I do not blame anyone or feel bitter, because families are often complicated.

I invited them to Martha’s Vineyard for a short getaway, and we arranged the timing together over several days. During the visit, we saw llamas grazing peacefully in nearby fields, enjoyed some excellent food, and visited places that were new to me as well. The whole trip moved quickly, making it difficult to pause and appreciate how fortunate I was. Everything felt like a whirlwind, and by the end I found myself wishing the time together did not have to end.

response: Today was an especially good day at my new job, which I value more than I ever expected. Six months ago, however, I believed my life had fallen apart after I resigned without another position or a clear plan. Looking back, I recognize that the decision was impulsive, although it seemed necessary at the time. I had been repeatedly harassed by a coworker named Jan, whose behavior toward people was rude, inappropriate, and largely ignored by the rest of the staff. During the office Christmas party, I stayed behind to finish a project while others socialized. Jan, who appeared intoxicated, repeatedly entered my office, urged me to drink and dance with her, and refused to leave after I asked several times. She continued touching me and bothering me despite my clearly stated requests for space.

response: Earlier this year, my grandmother passed away at the age of ninety-four, during Memorial Day weekend. Although she had told us she felt ready to die, losing her was still deeply painful. In the final weeks, she became increasingly frail and stayed in a nursing home. During my last visit, she remained asleep the entire time and never responded, yet I spoke softly to her, said that I loved her, and wished her peaceful, sweet dreams. That small farewell brought me some comfort. When the family called to tell me she was gone, I had not been shocked, though the loss continues to weigh on me. She was a fascinating woman, born in the United States to parents who had immigrated from Belgium.

response: I retired six months ago, after spending thirteen years serving customers at a pleasant family restaurant. This was my second retirement. I decided to leave because I had become too old to keep lifting loaded trays and completing the cleaning and other side duties that every employee was required to finish daily. response: I went to the hospital for cervical-spine surgery, during which doctors cut into the side of my neck and inserted hardware to fuse three vertebrae. The hospital treated those symptoms for four days before transferring me to a rehabilitation hospital to rebuild my strength and balance. I also became worried about the air we were breathing. Whenever the heating system operated, I noticed dust emerging from the ductwork, which concerned me because the house was quite old. I worked five days each week and spent most weekends at my aunt’s house, following that routine for nearly a year. Then, on an ordinary weekend visit, I noticed him there for the first time. His face and personality were unfamiliar to me, yet I immediately felt an unusual connection. It seemed like love at first sight because he was impressive, kind, and naturally warm toward everyone around him.

response: This occurred on St. Patrick’s Day in March 2019. I lived roughly twenty minutes from the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino in Tampa, Florida. For the holiday, the casino buffet was offering a special menu featuring several Irish-style foods, including shepherd’s pie, corned beef with cabbage, and fish and chips. Because my father’s birthday was approaching, I intended to take both of my parents there for a meal. We planned to arrive as soon as the buffet opened, since the holiday promotion usually attracted a crowd. However, my father apparently forgot about the plan and ate a substantial breakfast earlier that morning. As a result, he decided not to come, and the outing with my parents was canceled.

response: I am a grandmother with a thirty-year-old son. He married when he was seventeen, and he has two children: an eleven-year-old granddaughter and a two-year-old grandson. Both children are partly Jewish because their father’s father was Jewish and came from Poland, although he was born in New York in 1966. He later died from a brain tumor. My son appears healthy, but both of his children were born with brain cysts. They have each undergone brain surgery, yet the cysts remain and continue to affect their daily lives. They need regular medical appointments and monitoring. Only a week ago, my young grandson had another operation. I visited him in the hospital afterward, and he looked extremely fragile. His face was bluish and very pale, which made the situation especially upsetting for me.

response: Three weeks ago, I received upsetting news about two children who had previously been in our foster care, Mark and Sarah. I was sitting beside my husband on the couch when someone called to tell me that their mother had been arrested for breaking and entering. I felt devastated because we had always wanted the children to be safe and cared for. Their mother had seemed to be making positive changes, and I honestly believed she had left her former lifestyle behind. Hearing about the arrest made me question what would happen next, including whether I might need to return to fostering them. Since their mother can no longer provide reliable care, the children may need support again.

response: One afternoon in late June, I headed toward my neighborhood post office carrying a package that I intended to mail. Along the route, I noticed a sign advertising a blood donation drive taking place that day, and it said that additional donors were urgently needed. Although I had never donated blood before, I spontaneously decided to enter. The volunteers and nurses first asked me to complete a questionnaire and conducted the usual screening. After I passed, they allowed me to donate. Everything during the donation went smoothly, and the procedure lasted roughly fifteen minutes. When it ended, I sat nearby with a cookie and a cup of apple juice. I initially felt normal, but only a few minutes later I became lightheaded and dizzy.

response: I read about a woman whose cells profoundly influenced science, medicine, and vaccine research. In her thirties, she developed cervical cancer, and doctors removed a piece of her tumor to test whether its cells could survive in laboratory culture. Instead of dying, the cells multiplied rapidly and continued reproducing, leading scientists to describe them as immortal. The most emotionally striking part, though, was learning what caused her illness. Her cervical cancer was linked to repeated exposure to several strains of HPV transmitted by her husband. This connection was not recognized until many years later, which made the account especially memorable and disturbing.

response: About three or four months ago, I injured my arm when I fell out of bed. The bed was a metal-bar futon, and as I fell, it trapped me against the wall. Fortunately, my husband was home because I could not shift the heavy frame by myself. I yelled for him, and he came in quickly and pulled the bar away. My arm hurt quite a lot at first, but it did not appear to be fractured. Within the next day or two, a massive bruise spread across roughly half of my upper arm. Although it looked alarming, the pain had already become less severe. I treated the injury by applying ice during the first week. After that initial week, a hematoma gradually developed beneath the bruised area, even though the visible discoloration was beginning to seem less painful.

response: Approximately three months ago, I began seeing a therapist after spending a long time dealing privately with anxiety and depression. From the first appointment, I recognized that therapy was something I should have sought much earlier. During the third or fourth meeting, memories that I had kept buried for years began resurfacing. For the first time, I felt able to discuss them with someone who listened without judging me. There were no dismissive reactions, impatient eye rolls, or comments telling me to forget the past because it had happened long ago. I could describe whatever came into my mind, even when the memories were incomplete or difficult to organize, and I felt safe enough to continue speaking openly.

response: My father-in-law died on May 15, 2019, after several difficult years of declining health. He had been diagnosed with pulmonary disease in 2018, although his breathing problems may have started earlier. Despite being eighty years old, he remained energetic and continued living on the family farm, where he raised cattle and handled his daily chores. As his condition worsened, he gradually became unable to care for himself or maintain the farm. My husband and his brother eventually assumed those responsibilities. Because the rest of us lived about an hour away, the situation placed increasing strain on the entire family. His doctors gave him a poor prognosis, but he continued trying to persevere until his illness finally prevented him from working.

response: I never imagined I would reach this point, and I still question whether I made the right decision. I worry about whether Ben will manage well on his own, because he has had Asperger’s syndrome since childhood and I have always been protective of him. For years, he relied on me for nearly everything, and I considered it a privilege to meet even his smallest needs. My mind tells me that he is old enough to live independently and make his own choices, but my feelings are harder to quiet. Letting go is painful because caring for him has been such an important part of my life. Still, I believe the time has come for Ben to have more freedom, build confidence, and discover his own direction, even though I will continue to worry about him.

I remember the expression on his face when he heard the news: empty, still, and completely defeated. The doctors later said his heart had stopped for twelve minutes. Whether it was an extraordinary medical event or the result of my mother’s prayers, I do not know. He revived, however. My mother believed Jesus had saved him, and, unexpectedly, my father came to believe that too.

response: About three months ago, my daughter started kindergarten, and seeing her leave for her first school day felt like an important milestone in my life. I suddenly understood how my own mother must have felt when she sent me out into the world. I was proud and excited for my daughter, but I was also unusually anxious because I kept thinking that I would not be there to protect her. I realize that worrying cannot prevent anything, yet I still could not help it. It felt strange to remember experiencing kindergarten myself and then watch my child begin the same stage. She was eager that morning, while I managed only a few tears. I walked her to the classroom, and just before joining her friends, she hugged me tightly.

response: I believed I lived in a safe neighborhood because I had walked around town there for years without any problems. One day, however, a stranger suddenly grabbed me and appeared to try to kidnap me. The attack happened so quickly that I was caught off guard and could not react immediately. Fortunately, a nearby neighbor noticed what was happening, intervened, and helped me get free. The man ran away, so we contacted the police and filed a kidnapping report. The police are now searching for him. I am a middle-aged Korean man, and I know martial arts, so I believe I could eventually have defended myself, even though the attacker initially had control and the incident was unexpected.

response: Two months ago, I lost a substantial wager on a French Open tennis match. In recent months, I had been placing bets frequently, and the losses kept accumulating. I regret putting myself in this position, especially because I had promised that I would attend the French Open only as a spectator. Now I am unsure how I can replace the money I lost. I recognize that my gambling has become an addiction, and I believe I need professional help. Continuing this way will prevent me from saving for important goals, such as purchasing another car or eventually buying a home. I may need to stop attending sporting events altogether, since simply being somewhere that allows betting makes the temptation difficult to resist. Staying home would not solve everything, but it would remove some immediate opportunities and make it easier for me to avoid placing another bet.

response: My husband left his job at the post office roughly two months ago, after working there for thirty years. Although he had promised to remain employed until our car loan was completely paid, I did not feel ready for him to retire. The workplace had become increasingly hostile: supervisors and managers reportedly bullied staff daily and made the job unbearable. He and I attended counseling on several occasions, and he was prescribed medication to manage the strain. Eventually, however, he reached the point where continuing was no longer possible, so he resigned. His decision has created considerable stress for me as well. We are both too young to receive Social Security, and taking money from his retirement account before he turns fifty-nine and a half would result in a ten-percent penalty.

I contacted the veterinarian and started the long, difficult process of removing them, which took considerable time and effort. We named him Ash, inspired by the Pokemon master from my children’s favorite television show.

response: For many years, my life felt like a constant struggle. My wife and my son had both become dependent on alcohol, and I spent years trying to help them. I brought them to rehabilitation programs and to doctors, who prescribed different medications to help them stop drinking, but each improvement eventually faded. The financial burden also became overwhelming. Even though I earned a decent salary, medical bills and other expenses sometimes made it difficult to keep enough food in the house. Then, about six weeks ago, something changed in my thinking. After realizing that I could not control their choices or continue sacrificing myself indefinitely, I decided to stop seeing myself as helpless and to take responsibility for my own life.

response: A moment I will always remember was finally meeting my long-lost sister. We had been separated when we were very young, so for most of my childhood I knew almost nothing about her. I often asked my parents what she was like, whether they knew where she lived, and what she might be doing. Their limited answers only made me more curious and hopeful about meeting her someday. Eventually, I decided to search for her myself and see whether we could get in touch. My first efforts produced nothing, which was deeply disappointing. At the time, I interpreted that failure as a sign that finding her might be impossible and worried that I would never meet her in person. Even so, I kept thinking about her and did not completely abandon the possibility.

response: Our village has existed for generations beside a series of waterfalls. In recent years, hotel companies have repeatedly visited the area, apparently searching for suitable sites. From outside the village, the scenery is remarkable: the falls fill the air with mist that can be felt on your face. We live simply, but each person contributes through a particular role. We also bring in necessary goods and maintain active trade with people beyond the village. The elders remain doubtful about the proposed hotel development. Some residents believe it could create opportunities, enlarge the community, and bring in additional income from outside. Others fear that the hotel would employ us mainly as low-level workers, gradually turning residents into servants and eroding the customs and self-sufficient way of life we have maintained.

I had previously gone in with severe contractions, but the staff discharged me because I was only one centimeter dilated. Since then, I had barely slept for roughly two days, and every position was painful, whether sitting or lying down, so I spent most of the time standing. I also could not eat, and my irritated bladder made urinating nearly impossible. I felt more miserable than I ever had before. This time I was admitted, since the contractions had progressed my dilation from one centimeter to three.

I sang along with every song I knew and danced beside the other fans, who seemed equally familiar with the band’s music. response: I have a disability and have relied on a wheelchair for approximately seven years. Recently, though, I began an intensive effort to regain the ability to walk. With sustained treatment, I expect my strength to improve and walking with the walker to become less difficult.

response: At the end of May, I set out alone on a float trip intended to cover the entire Buffalo National River. It was a difficult choice because the river can be unpredictable, and I expected to spend hours without phone service or another person nearby. In practice, I often drifted near groups of fellow floaters, which made the journey feel less isolated. I met several kind people, and during the five nights I was away, two different groups invited me to share their campsites. Flooding eventually forced me to end the trip before reaching the full length of the river. Even so, the experience remains memorable, and completing the route is still on my bucket list. Although I traveled by myself, I never felt that I was truly in serious danger.

I had not witnessed an accident for several years, so the sudden crunch of metal and the sound of someone shouting were startling. We pulled over safely, turned on our hazard lights, and approached cautiously. One driver was sitting behind the wheel, visibly shaken and suffering from an injury, while another woman stood nearby calling for assistance. She told us that she knew the injured driver, although we could not tell whether she had been in the car when it crashed. Because frightened bystanders sometimes hesitate during emergencies, my friend and I asked whether help was needed and stayed there until emergency responders arrived. It felt fortunate that we happened to be present.

I can work full-time again, see my friends and family more often, and return to hobbies that had been pushed aside. Instead of traveling repeatedly to dialysis, I can now hike, take vacations, and enjoy ordinary moments with people I love. The change has been enormous, and everyday freedom feels precious.

I was involved in getting the program started around 2009, although I do not remember every part of how that happened. This summer, I took over a team that had been losing and tried to make it the fourth championship team in the program’s history. The season seemed to begin reasonably well, and the players appeared to respond to the practices and the stronger competition. We ended up as the second seed in our division and perhaps sixth overall among roughly 45 teams. Then things went badly when we lost to a team we had beaten several times before, although I cannot recall the exact scores or dates.

response: Two weeks ago, my niece was born unexpectedly while I was at home by myself. My sister-in-law, who lives just around the block, called me in a panic and said she was feeling painful contractions. She was 38 weeks pregnant, so I initially thought she might only be experiencing Braxton Hicks contractions, but I went over immediately. When I arrived, I saw a clear puddle spreading across the floor near her feet, and it became obvious that her water had broken. She did not want an ambulance because the paramedics would take her to the nearest hospital rather than her chosen hospital. Since she was uncomfortable and needed help quickly, I drove her there myself, trying to stay calm while she gathered her things.

response: Two weeks ago, what felt like an unusually long fourteen days began when my boyfriend’s mother went to her longtime doctor for a routine checkup. She expected nothing unusual because she had felt completely well and had noticed no chest pain, shortness of breath, or other warning signs. The initial tests led to additional, more advanced testing, and the results showed blockages in her arteries. The diagnosis surprised everyone, especially her, because she had trusted this doctor for years and believed she was healthy. After discussing the results and possible treatments, the doctor explained that a stent procedure was necessary. Later, she asked the family to sit together in the living room and told us what had happened. We were shocked and deeply upset.

When doctors diagnosed me with cancer, I feared I would not survive until the ceremony scheduled for June. That possibility broke my heart and filled me with regret. My older daughter proposed holding a small practice wedding beforehand, so I could experience the vows and celebration while I was still well enough. I decided to enroll in martial arts classes so I could feel more prepared. On my first evening, I was nervous because I was clearly the oldest person in the room. Instead of excluding me, the other students welcomed me, introduced themselves, and practiced beside me. He stopped somewhere overnight, probably at a truck stop, and some of the frozen chicken in the trailer was taken. I cannot remember how many boxes were missing, but it was not everything. response: For several years, I played bass with a band that was reasonably well known and traveled internationally, although it ended a few years back. I think we reunited last July and went somewhere in Colombia to perform. It was probably enjoyable, and somewhat strange, to work with the other members again after such a long break. We seemed to fall back into our usual habits fairly quickly, which was maybe funny. response: Sometimes the best thing that happens in life can also feel like the worst. Five months ago, my financial situation changed when my mortgage suddenly increased because of a balloon payment. I had heard the term before, but I did not understand that it meant a much larger payment could come due all at once. I remember staring at the new figure on my bank statement and realizing that my usual budget could not cover it. Normally, I would have worked overtime or taken an extra shift to manage an unexpected expense. Instead, this problem forced me to examine my finances carefully and discover an option I had overlooked, much like finding a hidden treasure map behind an accidental hole in a wall.

response: My son asked his girlfriend to marry him on August 11, 2019, during a family vacation. He proposed somewhere on the beach, and everyone was very happy about it. I started thinking about my own marriage and how I had been with my wonderful wife for thirty-five years. Since my son was beginning that part of life, I wondered whether it might be nice to propose to my wife again and renew our vows. We were visiting my father in the town where my wife and I had grown up. We had originally married in a United Methodist church there, so I suggested taking a drive to look around and see whether the town had changed. While driving, we happened to pass the church. I then suggested that we go inside for a little while and see if anything looked different. I thought it could be a suitable place to revisit our marriage.

response: I am writing about a medical experience that I have had for as long as I can remember. I think I have some kind of fainting disorder, and my doctor believed it could possibly be POTS. For some reason, I guess it took several months before a cardiologist finally ordered the relevant test. They seemed to check for nearly everything else first, although I am not sure exactly what was done. Eventually, I went to a hospital that dealt with heart problems and had what I think was called a tilt table test. They strap you to a table with something behind your head, let you lie there, and then raise the table to an angle that is probably below 90 degrees. You wait to see whether symptoms happen.

response: Two months ago, during a hot July, my dog died after an incident involving my other dog. I remember my surviving dog crying, and I held him while we cried together. I still think about the good times we had, especially our visits to the park. I used to throw a ball toward the soccer field, and once he accidentally grabbed a soccer ball. I kicked it back to the players, who were waiting nearby. He also loved peanut butter, so I sometimes mixed a little into his food. After eating it, he would smack his lips and drink a lot of water, which always made me smile. He had a happy, full life, and I hope he is resting peacefully in dog heaven. He was a good boy.

response: Four months ago, my wife and I traveled to Taiwan to visit her mother, who was receiving treatment for cancer. When we arrived, I hugged her tightly, and we both cried after hearing the latest medical news. We discussed our lives: my wife had recently been promoted, doubling her salary and adding vacation days, while I had finished a new product that should soon appear in stores. Her mother spent most of the visit lying in bed. Later, the doctor came in and explained that the cancer had worsened. The room became quiet, and we realized we had to leave. At the airport, my wife held my hand, and neither of us knew whether we would ever see her mother again.

response: Three weeks ago, I was sitting on our gray living-room couch beside my husband when my phone rang. The call concerned our former foster children, Mark and Sarah. response: I read a book about a woman whose cells apparently influenced science, medicine, and vaccines. She supposedly had cervical cancer when she was in her thirties, and doctors took some tumor tissue to see whether it might survive in culture. As I understand it, the cells continued living and multiplied unusually well, so they are now described as immortal. The part I found most memorable was the explanation of how she may have developed the cancer. It was later suggested that repeated exposure to different HPV strains from her husband was involved, although this was not recognized until many years afterward.

They arranged for me to meet a mentor, explaining that he was a middle-aged man who had also experienced difficulties as a teenager and could therefore understand what I was going through. At first, I resisted because I did not believe I needed anyone’s help. After thinking about how often my choices led to trouble, however, I agreed to try meeting him. My first impression was not especially positive, and I assumed we would not get along. Soon, though, he discovered that we shared interests in sports and video games. By the end of our first day together, I had changed my mind and thought he was actually a pretty cool person.

response: Coping with my mother’s death a month ago has been extremely difficult, and my entire family is struggling as well. Today, I decided to take a leave of absence from medical school because my depression has made it impossible to concentrate during classes and clinical rotations. I feel disappointed that I will fall behind my friends and classmates, yet I understand that stepping away is necessary for my well-being and for my mother. She always hoped I would become a doctor, which has been my dream too. This break will give me time to regain a healthier mental state so I can eventually return and become a capable physician. When I resume my studies, I will have three semesters remaining.

For some reason, it took several months before a cardiologist arranged the appropriate testing. Before that happened, the doctors appeared to check me for nearly every other possible problem. Eventually, I went to a cardiac hospital for a tilt table test. During this procedure, you are secured to a table and supported by a pillow under your head. He was traveling and hoped to stop by for a visit. It was hard to believe, since our busy schedules during the past year had kept us from seeing each other. I devoted far too much time to cleaning and organizing the house before he arrived, and, as usual, I went overboard baking all kinds of sweets. Still, gaining a few pounds seemed like a small price to pay for enjoying ourselves together.

response: July 18, 2019, will always be etched in my heart, although this story really started on July 3, 2017. While browsing Craigslist, I came across a video of a small, cream-colored puppy. His eleven siblings were energetically playing and climbing over him, and in the next scene they were still piled on top of him. I immediately felt that he was the one. My husband and I brought him home for $60, only to discover that he was covered in fleas. I contacted the veterinarian and began the challenging process of removing them. The treatment was tedious and time-consuming. We named him Ash, after the Pokemon master from my children’s favorite show.

response: For many years, my life has felt like an ongoing battle. Both my wife and my son have been consumed by alcohol addiction. I brought them to rehabilitation programs and to doctors, who prescribed different medications intended to help them overcome their drinking. Unfortunately, none of these efforts produced lasting results, and the costs continued to grow. Even with a decent income, I was struggling to afford basic food for the family. Then, six weeks ago, I realized I had to stop seeing myself as a victim.

response: One unforgettable moment in my life was finally meeting my long-lost sister. We had been separated when we were very young, so I grew up knowing almost nothing about her. I often asked my parents what she was like, whether they knew where she was, and what she might be doing. Listening to them describe her made me increasingly curious and hopeful that we would someday meet in person. Eventually, I decided to investigate on my own and search for information that might help me contact her. Unfortunately, my efforts produced no results. At the time, that failure was deeply painful because I began to believe that if I could not locate her then, I might never have the chance to meet her at all.

response: I now spend most of my time on the island of Bali, having retired last year. Winters in the United States feel too cold for me, which is one reason I prefer being there. Since I had only arrived in Bali the month before, I immediately had to turn around and return to be with her. response: Our village has existed for many years beside the waterfalls. During the past several years, I have noticed hotel companies looking around for suitable sites. From outside the village, the scenery is stunning, and you can feel the waterfall’s mist on your face. We live simply, with every person contributing through a particular role. We also bring in the goods we need and maintain productive trade with people from beyond the village. The elders remain uncertain about whether welcoming a hotel chain would be wise. Some villagers believe the development could help us grow and bring in greater income from outsiders. Others fear that we would merely become hotel employees, gradually abandoning our traditions and way of life as we were reduced to serving the visitors.

response: The date was July 29, 2019, my official due date. A few days earlier, I had gone to the hospital because my contractions were unbearable, but they sent me home when they found I was only one centimeter dilated. Since then, the pain had been so intense that I had barely slept for about 48 hours. Sitting and lying down both hurt, so I had spent nearly two days standing. I also had not been able to eat. To make matters worse, my bladder became irritated and stopped functioning properly, leaving me unable to urinate despite trying repeatedly. I felt more miserable than ever. Eventually, I could not tolerate it any longer, so my mother and boyfriend brought me back to the hospital. Thankfully, I was admitted after dilating to three centimeters, apparently because of all those intense contractions!

Fortunately, I often found myself near groups of fellow floaters. Along the way, I met several kind people, and I was even invited to join their camps on two occasions during my five nights on the river. Although I traveled alone, I was never truly in danger.

response: Generally speaking, my girlfriend and I rarely fight, and any disagreements we do have usually involve minor topics that typical couples experience. However, a fortnight ago, a conflict arose regarding my reluctance to spend time with her companions. Because I genuinely find them irritating, I was honest about it. I assumed this dynamic was standard in relationships. Unfortunately, she felt deeply offended, arguing that criticizing her social circle is equivalent to attacking her personal identity. The situation escalated unnecessarily. She even attempted to back me into a corner by asking illogical questions, such as whether my dislike for her friends means I also find her annoying.

response: During the month of June, my dad contacted me to propose a road trip to Yellowstone National Park. This came as a massive shock since we had been completely estranged for more than a decade. Our last interaction ended on very poor terms because of serious disagreements back when we lived in the same neighborhood. I was utterly astonished that he initiated contact and proposed such an activity. Furthermore, he extended an invitation to my romantic partner of six years, despite them never having met each other. Because of my profound surprise, I did not provide an immediate response during our initial conversation. Instead, I felt it was necessary to discuss the entire situation with both my girlfriend and my mental health therapist to determine whether accepting this invitation would actually be a wise choice.

response: Ever since we lost our beloved dog Buddy to liver cancer two months ago, my heart has been completely broken, and my life has not been the same. In retrospect, his health had clearly started declining late last year, but I completely missed the warning signs at the time. Initially, he experienced increased vomiting and slight weight loss, which I naively attributed to normal aging. However, everything changed when I found him resting uncomfortably and struggling to sleep. I rushed him to the veterinarian, and when the staff escorted me into that dreaded consultation room, time completely froze. The diagnosis was advanced liver cancer with virtually no chance of recovery. That moment completely shattered me, as Buddy truly meant everything to me.

response: Several of my close companions successfully overcame their battles against cancer. To celebrate their recovery and embrace life fully, our entire friend group planned a vacation together on a cruise ship. We gave the two cancer survivors complete authority to choose the destination, and they ultimately decided on a fantastic Caribbean voyage. Our trip lasted for seven days, during which we visited five unique ports of call. Every single day was filled with exciting excursions and joyful celebrations. Additionally, one of our single friends met an amazing man during the journey. They are still in a serious relationship today. We even bought two wonderful artworks at an onboard auction.

response: During the initial weekend of July, I managed to accomplish something that had been completely out of my reach for more than twenty-five years. For the very first time since my early twenties, I got the chance to participate in drag racing once again. Although simply getting back on the track was an incredible milestone on its own, the fact that I was actually competing in a major national event made it extraordinarily special. Participating in a competition of that scale had always remained a distant lifelong dream of mine. Because I honestly never expected to afford my own professional race car, I previously considered the entire idea utterly impossible. However, roughly a fortnight prior to the official start of the race, a wonderful close friend completely surprised me by revealing that he had always been well aware of my burning passion for racing and desperately wanted to help turn that aspiration into a reality.

response: Late in the month of May, I embarked on a solo floating excursion with the ambitious goal of navigating the complete stretch of the Buffalo National River. Making this choice was quite difficult because unexpected hazards can easily arise, leaving a person entirely isolated for hours without any visible companionship or cellular reception. Fortunately, I frequently found myself surrounded by friendly fellow travelers. This fortunate circumstance allowed me to connect with wonderful individuals and receive two camping invitations during my five-night journey. Although rising floodwaters ultimately prevented me from finishing the entire route, the unforgettable memories will stay with me forever. Successfully accomplishing this major bucket list dream remains a top priority for me. Even though I traveled alone, I fortunately never faced any genuine danger.

response: Back in May, I welcomed my first baby girl into the world. Having two very young boys already made me extremely nervous about welcoming a third child so soon. Even though I typically enjoy being pregnant, this particular journey proved quite difficult on both my physical health and mental well-being. Chasing after a toddler and a one-year-old on a daily basis left me continually exhausted. Although my partner and I originally intended to wait several years before expanding our family further, discovering that unexpected positive test came as a massive shock. I spent the entire pregnancy overwhelmed and anxious. The moment she finally arrived, my perspective shifted completely.
